root_cause_note: P19 (NASDAQ:AMAL, Amalgamated Financial Corp.) is the US half of the in-app AMAL ticker collision; P9 (BSE 506597, Amal Ltd) is the Indian half (see manifest.json). collected.calls.resolve_bare_symbol shows the resolver finds BOTH instruments at identical confidence 1.0 for a bare 'AMAL' query but binds silently to the India candidate (needs_disambiguation:false) because the active request region defaults to IN and sidecar/services/resolution_policy.py documents cross-region exact ties as NOT residual (bind stands, D58b). /quotes/{symbol}, /fundamentals/{symbol}, /fundamentals/{symbol}/ratings, /disclosures/shareholding and /disclosures/announcements expose no region/exchange parameter at all (only /resolve and /fundamentals/{symbol}/narrative do), so every one of those routes re-resolves 'AMAL' from scratch and lands on Amal Ltd (BSE), even though this collection's SLOT is explicitly the US company. Only /fundamentals/AMAL/income, /balance and /cashflow (openbb-mcp, which ignores the sidecar's own resolver/region entirely per DAT-P9-1) happen to return real US-company data for this slot. See raw findings DAT-P19-1..3 for the mechanism.

fields.note: collected.calls.resolve_bare_symbol.body.resolved.name and calls.fundamentals.body.name both read 'Amal Ltd' — the Indian BSE 506597 chemicals maker, not the slot's intended NASDAQ bank holding company. See DAT-P19-1.

fields.note: One of the few rows where the app's silence is actually correct: it does not fabricate a rename, and neither does the pack after investigation.

Pack: identity.isin.value is structurally absent for a US issuer (SEC does not publish ISIN; pack.world_gaps.structurally_absent lists identity.isin explicitly) — the correct app answer for this slot is null/absent. Instead the app confidently returns a real ISIN, INE841D01013, belonging to the wrong (Indian) company. Treated as a mismatch, not 'no source truth', because the app is not silent here — it asserts a concrete, wrong value.
Pack: not_applicable (US-listed issuer, no BSE code exists). App asserts a real BSE code for the wrong company. Same pattern as identity.isin above.
Both sides null for the same reason (no NSE symbol exists for a US issuer); not a finding.

fields.outside_value: Nasdaq Global Market (NASDAQ-GM), not Global Select
fields.note: Two stacked defects: (1) the bare query resolves to the wrong exchange entirely (BSE, not US); (2) even the correctly name-resolved candidate only carries a bare 'US' exchange string — the resolver/Instrument schema has no market-tier field, so 'Nasdaq Global Market' vs 'Global Select' could never be represented even on a correct resolution.

collected.calls.fundamentals.body.dividend_per_share_ttm = null. The field exists in the schema (unlike the date fields above) and is designed exactly for this — 'trailing-12m dividends ACTUALLY PAID' (fundamentals.py comment) is precisely the declared-vs-paid distinction the pack's #1 critical trap is built around — but it is never populated for this slot.

Two stacked defects: wrong company/currency, AND field_meta.fifty_two_week_high.as_of carries only the API-call timestamp (2026-09-19T10:00:06Z), never the date the high actually printed — a value can be right and its date wrong, or (here) both wrong. Mandatory subtle-tier field per the DIFF spec.
Same as week52.high: wrong entity plus no per-leg as-of date.

fields.app_value: quarter_end 2026-06-30, promoter_percent 71.35, fii_percent null, dii_percent 0.03, public_percent 28.65 (all real BSE-filed values, for Amal Ltd)
fields.note: Pack: shareholding.promoter_pct/fii_pct/dii_pct/public_pct are ALL null with pack.world_gaps.structurally_absent — 'promoter' and the FII/DII split are SEBI-only concepts with no US disclosure regime, so per the DIFF spec ('no outside value -> no source truth, never a raw finding') this row is not a mismatch. The app's behaviour is still a genuine defect — see DAT-P19-2 in the raw findings file — but it is filed as a standalone identity/data-trust finding, not as a field mismatch, because the strict per-field rule has nothing to diff against.
Structurally absent on both sides for a US issuer; the BSE shareholding schema itself also has no pledge field (a separate, India-scope gap already out of scope here).
